speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand your condition, can you describe what the spinning sensation feels like and how long each episode lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Given your age and the sudden, position-dependent nature of these episodes, have you noticed any associated ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or a feeling of fullness in your head during the dizziness? REQUEST TEST: Audiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere's disease or labyrinthitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Head Impulse Test (HIT).
Please also report if you have experienced any transient weakness, numbness, or double vision during your episodes.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (Posterior Fossa) if HIT is abnormal or symptoms atypical.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Head Impulse Test (HIT): Normal (no corrective saccades observed). No transient weakness, numbness, or double vision reported during episodes. MRI Brain (Posterior Fossa): No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest central causes of vertigo.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good news; the normal Head Impulse Test and MRI effectively rule out central causes like a stroke. Since your vertigo is position-dependent, have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or difficulty walking when these episodes occur?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical picture of position-dependent vertigo, normal hearing tests (ruling out Meniere's), and a normal Head Impulse Test and MRI (ruling out central causes) is diagnostic for BPPV.
